name: Layered Cutout Infographic Scene
use_when: An explainer needs a final or transition graphic built from cutout objects, title text, and editorial background layers.
A building, person, animal, object, product, or symbol can represent the topic more clearly than a flat title card.
The sequence needs a polished collage scene without leaving CapCut or the NLE.
A documentary scene needs multiple cutouts to fade, overlap, and move through a shallow parallax composition.
avoid_when: The cutout asset is low resolution, uncleared, or misleading.
The scene uses official logos, public figures, or institutional imagery in a way that implies endorsement.
A simpler document, chart, or map would communicate the point more directly.

timeline_pattern.pattern: background -> keyed_or_auto_cutout_1 -> cutout_2 -> title_text_panel -> staggered_slide_or_wipe -> compound -> subtle_zoom_rotation -> exit
timeline_pattern.cutout_rule: Remove backgrounds cleanly and inspect edges before animating.
timeline_pattern.hierarchy_rule: The main cutout or title should read first; supporting cutouts enter after.
timeline_pattern.compound_rule: Group the scene once internal timing is working so the whole collage can zoom, rotate, or transition together.
timeline_pattern.fade_overlap_rule: Overlap fade-outs and fade-ins when one cutout should hand off to another instead of cutting to unrelated stills.

motion.rule: Use simple slide, wipe, fade, scale, and slight rotation so collage motion feels editorial rather than chaotic.

keyframe_values.compound_zoom: Use a small push-in, often 3-8%, when the scene needs life after elements enter.
keyframe_values.rotation: Use slight rotation, around 1-3 degrees, only when it supports handmade editorial texture.
keyframe_values.edge_check: Review keyed cutout edges before applying low-FPS or texture effects.
keyframe_values.cutout_fade: A 0.5s fade-out can be a starting point for calm documentary cutout exits; shorten or lengthen by narration.

sound.rule: Use one or two soft whooshes, pops, or camera cues for major cutout/title entrances; avoid a cue on every layer.

captions.rule: Do not let subtitles collide with title panels or cutout subjects.

color.rule: Match cutouts to the paper/background palette enough that the collage feels intentional while preserving source recognizability.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use chromakey/alpha masks or pre-cut PNGs, overlay title panels, keyframe scale/position/rotation, and render edge-check frames.
implementation.remotion: Create a CutoutInfographicScene component with cutouts, titlePanel, entranceOrder, compoundTransform, edgeReviewFrames, and rights metadata.
implementation.blender: Use image planes with alpha, orthographic camera motion, and subtle rotation for a rendered collage scene.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use chroma key or auto removal for cutouts, add title text/background panels, apply slide/wipe/fade animations, overlap cutout fades, compound the scene, then keyframe zoom/rotation or pass the scene into a dedicated parallax collage workflow.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use keyed PNG/video layers, Essential Graphics panels, Linear Wipe/Position animations, nested sequence transforms, and edge/caption QC.

common_mistakes: Using cutouts with messy edges or obvious background remnants.
Animating all cutouts at once so hierarchy is unclear.
Using official or institutional imagery without considering rights and implied endorsement.
Rotating or zooming until labels/cutouts become hard to read.
Leaving the scene ungrouped so later timing changes desync layers.
Letting foreground cutouts cover title text until the documentary label cannot be read.
qc: Are all cutout assets licensed, attributed, or approved for the project?
Do keyed edges look clean before and after texture/FPS effects?
Does the viewer know which cutout or text to read first?
Do captions avoid title panels and cutout subjects?
Does the compound motion preserve all edges within frame?
Do fade overlaps make the cutout handoff feel intentional rather than like a random slideshow?
